rationale: Requires verifying that message content arrives unchanged, which is data integrity.
Identity and spending data must be kept from any reader other than the issuer, which is confidentiality.
Keeps serving while rejecting injection and brute-force floods from hostile clients, which is resistance to attack.
Forces periodic replacement of the sign-in credential before further sign-ins, a credential-management rule tied to authentication.
Requires a biometric identity match of the developer before signing, which is authentication.
Managers must prove identity with a valid credential before the screen is shown, which is authentication without a stated data-protection goal.
Hash comparison against the archived value reveals alteration of the report, which is integrity.
Sets a minimum strength for operator credentials, a rule about the authentication credential.
Blocks outbound telemetry that would disclose source code against disclosure rules, which protects confidentiality.
Idle-session closure explicitly aims to prevent an attacker from abusing an abandoned session (rule 7).
Obfuscation keeps embedded strings and licence keys from being read in the binary, which is protection against disclosure.
Only users presenting a valid registered identity token may submit jobs, which is identity verification.
Separate read and write permissions per component limit who can view and who can change data (rule 3).
Guest analysts get view-only access and all insert, update and delete attempts are blocked, restricting modification.
Requires that passport and payment details were protected against disclosure in transit and discards those that were not.
Returns only the needed patient fields and withholds the rest, limiting exposure of patient data.
An embedded integrity mark allows detection of later modification of the binary.
Requires stored data to remain correct and consistent with each committed statement, which is data integrity.
Encrypted link protocol prevents interception of content, with no mention of alteration detection (rule 5).
Digital signature check confirms the file's origin from an authorised consortium member and implies content integrity (rule 4).
Flags images whose embedded ownership mark was removed or changed, detecting alteration.
Clearing memory with camera streams and credentials prevents disclosure of leftover content.
Only holders of the forecast-editor role may create or change scenarios, restricting modification.
Validates ranges and formats and rejects inconsistent records, ensuring data accuracy and coherence.
Restricts to one role the power to change who may edit datasets, controlling modification rights.
Hash verification discards altered rule sets, detecting modification; no origin check is stated.
Requires a time-limited identity confirmation before the access credential can be replaced, which is identity verification.
Detecting presentation of a retired token is replay detection, which is resistance.
Each developer must be identified by a distinct credential before jobs are accepted, which is identification and authentication.
Requires commands to be executed exactly as specified with a matching device state, which is correctness of state with no attack stated.
Restricts viewing of node addresses and capacity to administrators, limiting read access.
A MAC over the balance history lets the terminal recognise tampering.
Hash comparison rejects datasets that differ from the recorded value, detecting alteration.
Enters a locked state on detecting fault-induction attacks, a secure state under malicious manipulation.
Format validation prevents malformed entries from corrupting stored records, protecting data integrity.
Salary values must be recorded exactly without unintended alteration, which is data integrity.
Reversal is accepted only if source and totals match the original load, protecting loaded data from improper modification.
Verifies the entered PIN against a stored reference before granting access, which is authentication.
Verifies the analyst's X.509 certificate at sign-in and reuses the verified identity, which is authentication.
